tasks.instruction: Write a discussion response. An effective response contains at least 100 words.

professor.name: Dr. Achebe
professor.text: Let's continue talking about consumer behavior. We have been discussing different ways people go about choosing what products to buy, and there are many potential sources of information and advice for consumers. In your opinion, which is the better strategy for making purchasing decisions, relying on advice from friends and family, or depending on information from online sources? Why?

posts.name: Claire
posts.text: Asking friends and family members for product recommendations might seem like an easier option, but it might take too much time to get all the information you need. An internet search would be much more efficient. There are many consumer magazines available online that compile lots of data to compare the advantages and disadvantages of one product versus another.

posts.name: Paul
posts.text: The last time I bought a computer, I just watched a few videos online to make a decision, and now I regret that. My friends could have advised me better because they know my preferences and the kind of features that I am interested in. Consumers should get advice from the people around them to get the most suitable products.

tasks.sample:
From my perspective, it is better to acquire information from online resources than from friends and family when making purchasing decisions.

To begin with, online information is more comprehensive and accurate. Nowadays, there are numerous content creators writing reviews or making testing videos, which are good sources of information because many of them have pertinent expertise and professional equipment. For example, there are videos online comparing different cellphones from all major brands like Apple, Samsung, Xiaomi, and Huawei in laboratory experiments. The products are tested on all aspects, ranging from appearance to durability and signal strength. By contrast, family and friends do not likely have laboratories and all those phones.

Moreover, it is easier to get information from online resources. When people want to know about any product, they only need to visit certain websites to check tremendous information like professional analysis and authentic customer reviews, spending several minutes. Meanwhile, asking for advice from friends and family can be more time-consuming. Having their own things to attend to, they may not be able to respond immediately. Plus, exchanging messages can also take longer than just browsing pages online.

In conclusion, online resources are more helpful when people want to buy something.
